title: O God, Thy Grace Impart
description: O God, Thy Grace Impart in Tonic Solfa to MALVERN (GWYLLT), doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Ray Palmer wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 335 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “For Divine Guidance”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sixes and Fours (6.6.4.6.6.6.4), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MALVERN (GWYLLT); any other Sixes and Fours tune fits them as well.
underlay: O God, thy grace im-part! Re-vive my faint-ing heart; My zeal in-spire; Re-veal thy-self to me, And may my love to thee Pure, warm, and change-less be, A liv-ing fire.

lines: And may my love to thee
While life's dark maze I tread,

licence: Public domain: Ray Palmer died in 1887.
credits: Words by Ray Palmer (1808–1887), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MALVERN (GWYLLT) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
